content.title: Assessment of venous thromboembolism recurrence risk (Section 8.1)
content.source_summary: Landmark clinical trials evaluated durations of anticoagulant treatment with VKAs for VTE and permit several conclusions.
key_conclusions: All patients with PE should receive at least 3 months of anticoagulant treatment.
After withdrawal of anticoagulant treatment, risk of recurrence is expected to be similar if anticoagulants are stopped after 3–6 months compared with longer treatment periods (e.g., 12–24 months).
Extended oral anticoagulant treatment reduces the risk for recurrent VTE by approximately 90%, but this benefit is partially offset by an increased risk of bleeding.
Oral anticoagulants are highly effective in preventing recurrent VTE during treatment, but they do not eliminate the risk of subsequent recurrence after discontinuation.
content.clinical_question: How to best select candidates for extended or indefinite anticoagulation, balancing recurrence risk and bleeding risk, with patient involvement in decision-making.
content.recurrence_risk_data: A cited study following patients after a first episode of acute PE reported recurrence rates after discontinuation of treatment; the guideline text reports numeric recurrence rates (text contains garbled characters in the image) and specifically notes 4.5% per year cited for PE occurring in the absence of known cancer, known thrombophilia, or any transient risk factor.
risk_group_classification: Patients with a strong (major) transient or reversible risk factor (eg, major surgery or trauma) — often considered responsible for the index episode.
Patients in whom the index episode might be partly explained by a weak (minor) transient or reversible risk factor, or if a non-malignant risk factor for thrombosis persists.
Patients in whom the index episode occurred in the absence of any identifiable risk factor (guidelines avoid terms such as 'unprovoked' or 'idiopathic').
Patients with one or more previous episodes of VTE and those with a major persistent pro-thrombotic condition such as antiphospholipid antibody syndrome.
content.tables_and_references: Table 11 shows examples of transient/reversible and persistent risk factors for VTE, classified by risk of long-term recurrence. Section 8.4 is dedicated to management of PE in patients with cancer.
content.practice_implication: When deciding on duration of anticoagulation, consider index PE features, presence/absence of transient or persistent risk factors (including cancer or antiphospholipid syndrome), bleeding risk, and patient preferences.
